def-csm-frontier-local-topologies:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a finite nonempty alphabet $S$ with the discrete topology, and a bijective enumeration $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ of $\mathbb Z^d$. Let $\Omega=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ be the set of all configurations $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to S$ with the product topology, the smallest topology that makes each coordinate map $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_x$ continuous. For a finite set $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and assignment $a\in S^F$, the cylinder set determined by $(F,a)$ is $[F,a]=\{\sigma\in\Omega:\sigma|_F=a\}$. The cylinder sigma-algebra $\mathcal C$ is generated by these sets.

For each finite $F$, let $\pi_F:\Omega\to S^F$ be restriction to $F$. For probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal C)$, local weak convergence $\mu_n\to_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu$ means that $(\pi_F)_*\mu_n(B)\to(\pi_F)_*\mu(B)$ for every finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and every $B\subseteq S^F$. Equivalently, all finite-coordinate cylinder probabilities converge. The cylinder sigma-algebra is shown below in a local result to equal the Borel sigma-algebra, with local weak convergence equal to ordinary weak convergence on this space.
def-csm-frontier-vague-topology:
## Definition

Fix $d\ge1$. A locally finite counting measure on $\mathbb R^d$ is a measure of the form $\xi=\sum_{r\in I}\delta_{x_r}$, where $I$ is finite or countable, repetitions among the points $x_r\in\mathbb R^d$ are allowed, and every compact set contains only finitely many listed points, counting repetitions. The empty sum is allowed and is the zero measure. For a Borel set $B$, $\xi(B)$ is the number of listed points in $B$, with multiplicity. Write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ for the set of these measures. For $x\in\mathbb R^d$, the point mass $\delta_x$ assigns mass $1$ to a Borel set containing $x$ and mass $0$ otherwise.

The vague topology on $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ is the coarsest topology for which $\xi\mapsto\int f\,d\xi$ is continuous for every nonnegative continuous compactly supported function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$. Thus $\xi_n\to_{\mathrm v}\xi$ exactly when $\int f\,d\xi_n\to\int f\,d\xi$ for every such $f$.

Here a random locally finite counting measure means a measurable random element for which $\Xi_n(B)$ is a random variable for every bounded Borel set $B$. If $(\Xi_n)$ is a sequence of such measures on a common probability space and $K$ is compact, its local counts are uniformly integrable on $K$ when

$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_n\mathbb E\!\left[\Xi_n(K)\mathbf1_{\{\Xi_n(K)>R\}}\right]=0.$$

This is the count-tail condition used when an argument needs control of unbounded observables supported in $K$. The definition asserts no convergence of expectations without the exact test-function, support, and tail hypotheses of the result being applied.
def-csm-frontier-finite-generator-chain:
## Definition

Let $E=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for a finite integer $m\ge1$. A rate matrix on $E$ is a real matrix $L=(L_{ij})_{i,j\in E}$ such that $L_{ij}\ge0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\sum_{j\in E}L_{ij}=0$ for every $i$. Write $\lambda_i=\sum_{j\ne i}L_{ij}$, so $L_{ii}=-\lambda_i$. The row convention acts on a column observable $f:E\to\mathbb R$ by $(Lf)(i)=\sum_jL_{ij}f(j)$; a row probability vector evolves by right multiplication.

Fix an initial probability vector $\nu$ on $E$ and put $q=\max_i\lambda_i$. If $q=0$, then $L=0$ and the associated realization is the constant process $X_t=Y_0$ with $Y_0\sim\nu$. If $q>0$, put $R=I+L/q$, a stochastic matrix. A uniformized realization consists of a probability space carrying a discrete-time Markov sequence $(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ with initial law $\nu$ and transition matrix $R$, and independent random variables $(W_n)_{n\ge1}$ that are independent of the entire sequence $Y$ and satisfy $\mathbb P(W_n>u)=e^{-qu}$ for $u\ge0$. Here a discrete-time Markov sequence with transition matrix $R$ means that
$$\mathbb P(A\cap\{Y_{n+1}=j\})=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A R_{Y_nj}]$$
for every $n\ge0$, $j\in E$, and $A\in\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)$. Each $W_n$ therefore has the exponential distribution of rate $q$; in particular its mean is $q^{-1}$. Require $\sum_{n\ge1}W_n=+\infty$ almost surely. Put $T_0=0$, $T_n=\sum_{k=1}^nW_k$, and, on this probability-one event, $N_t=\max\{n:T_n\le t\}$ and $X_t=Y_{N_t}$. On its null complement set $N_t=0$ and $X_t=Y_0$. The construction filtration is $\mathcal F_t=\sigma(N_s,X_s:0\le s\le t)$; it records event counts and states through time $t$ and is not completed or made right-continuous by this definition.

This uniformized construction permits reducible rate matrices and states with zero exit rate. A local existence result proves that every finite rate matrix and initial law admit such a realization and that its conditional transition matrices are $e^{tL}:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty t^nL^n/n!$.
lem-csm-frontier-finite-doob-bound:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a real square-integrable martingale relative to a filtration $(\mathcal F_t)$, with càdlàg paths almost surely and $M_0=0$. Then
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|^2\right]\le4\,\mathbb E[|M_T|^2].$$
lem-csm-frontier-finite-entropy-chain:
## Statement

Let $I,J$ be finite nonempty sets, let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on $I\times J$, and assume $Q(x,y)>0$ for every $(x,y)$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on a finite set with $q$ strictly positive, define
$$D(p\|q)=\sum_{z:p(z)>0}p(z)\ln\frac{p(z)}{q(z)},$$
with zero-mass terms omitted. Let $P_X,Q_X$ be the first-coordinate marginals. For $x$ with $P_X(x)>0$, let $P_{Y|x},Q_{Y|x}$ be the conditional probability vectors; terms weighted by $P_X(x)=0$ are omitted. Then
$$D(P\|Q)=D(P_X\|Q_X)+\sum_{x:P_X(x)>0}P_X(x)D(P_{Y|x}\|Q_{Y|x}).$$
For every subset $C\subseteq I\times J$, grouping the atoms into $C$ and its complement cannot increase relative entropy:
$$D(P\|Q)\ge d(P(C)\|Q(C)),\qquad d(a\|b)=a\ln\frac ab+(1-a)\ln\frac{1-a}{1-b},$$
with zero-weight terms omitted and the empty/full event cases interpreted as equality.
lem-csm-frontier-cylinder-weak-equivalen:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $S$ be a finite nonempty set with a fixed total order, and fix a bijective enumeration $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ of $\mathbb Z^d$. Put $\Omega=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$, give it the product topology, and let its cylinder sigma-algebra be generated by finite-coordinate assignments. Then the product topology is induced by
$$\rho(\sigma,\eta)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-k}\mathbf1_{\{\sigma_{x_k}\ne\eta_{x_k}\}},$$
$\Omega$ is compact, and its Borel sigma-algebra equals the cylinder sigma-algebra. For probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on this sigma-algebra, convergence of every finite-coordinate marginal is equivalent to weak convergence, where weak convergence means convergence of integrals of every bounded continuous real function on $\Omega$.
lem-csm-frontier-finite-generator-chain-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ be a nonempty finite set, let $L$ be a rate matrix on $E$ with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums, and let $\nu$ be an initial probability vector. Then there exists a uniformized realization under the conventions stated below. Its paths are càdlàg and almost surely have only finitely many event times on each bounded interval (nonexplosion), and, for all $0\le s\le t$,
$$\mathbb P(X_t=j\mid\mathcal F_s)=(e^{(t-s)L})_{X_sj}\quad\text{almost surely},$$
where $\mathcal F_s=\sigma(N_u,X_u:0\le u\le s)$ is the construction filtration. In particular, $e^{tL}$ is the transition matrix from any initial state.
lem-csm-frontier-finite-chain-martingale:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ be finite and nonempty, let $L$ be a rate matrix on $E$, let $X$ be its uniformized realization from the preceding existence result, and let $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be bounded. Put $g=Lf$ and
$$M_t=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t g(X_s)\,ds,\qquad \Gamma_f(i)=L(f^2)(i)-2f(i)Lf(i).$$For every finite $T$, $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ is a square-integrable martingale relative to the construction filtration, and$$A_t:=\int_0^t\Gamma_f(X_s)\,ds$$
is its continuous predictable bracket: $A_0=0$, $A$ is increasing and predictable, and $M_t^2-A_t$ is a martingale. The bracket is understood in the continuous predictable increasing compensator convention stated in the proof.
